root_cause.text: The i2c_imx_master_isr() unconditionally transitions the state to IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_CONTINUE after processing the block data length, overwriting any error state (IMX_I2C_STATE_FAILED) set by the length handler when an invalid block length is received, causing an endless read loop that overruns buffers and crashes the system.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a guard (`if (i2c_imx->state == IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_BLOCK_DATA_LEN)`) before setting the state to READ_CONTINUE, preserving the error state. The CVE description explicitly states: "i2c_imx_master_isr() unconditionally overwrites this with IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_CONTINUE, causing an endless read loop that overruns buffers and crashes the system."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential race or incorrect state transition by only advancing to READ_CONTINUE if the state hasn't been changed by the read block data length handler.
intent_record.what: Added an if condition to check that i2c_imx->state == IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_BLOCK_DATA_LEN before setting it to IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_CONTINUE.
intent_record.how: Previously, the state was unconditionally set to READ_CONTINUE after calling i2c_imx_isr_read_block_data_len. Now, the transition only occurs if the state remains READ_BLOCK_DATA_LEN, allowing the function to change the state (e.g., to IDLE or ERROR) without being overwritten, preventing incorrect handling of completed or failed block reads.

grouping_result.intent: Fix potential race or incorrect state transition by only advancing to READ_CONTINUE if the state hasn't been changed by the read block data length handler.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by modifying the state transition to only advance to READ_CONTINUE if the state hasn't been changed by the block data length handler, preventing overwriting of error states.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional assignment overwrites any error state (e.g., IMX_I2C_STATE_FAILED) that i2c_imx_isr_read_block_data_len may have set when an invalid block length is received, causing the state machine to continue reading instead of stopping, leading to buffer overrun and crash.
